--- name: issue-managing description: "How the project manager organizes, assigns, and tracks work through agentrack. Use whenever planning new work, triaging ideas, fixing stuck issues, or coordinating across teams. Defines the sync-tracker pattern, the strict issue hierarchy, parent-status rules, and a recipe for each loop (work / ideas / status) that keeps work flowing without micromanagement." --- # Issue Managing — How the PM Drives Work Through Agentrack You don't do the work — you **structure issues** so the work loop and other agents do. Structure the issues correctly and the system runs itself; get it wrong and work silently stalls. For the `agt` command reference, see the `agentrack` skill. ## How the work loop drives issues (read this first) Agentrack has a work loop that runs continuously. For every issue it asks three questions: 1. Status is `todo`? 2. Has an assignee? 3. Has no open blockages? If **all three are yes**, the loop hands the issue to the assignee. The assignee sets it `in-progress`, does the work, adds a comment with results, and marks it `done` (or back to `todo` assigned to you if they hit a problem). **When an issue is marked `done`, the system automatically clears every blockage that issue was causing.** You never run `agt blockages resolve` — the system does it for you. You only *create* blockages (`agt blockages add --by `) to sequence work. This auto-clear is the engine that makes a phase chain flow: Design done → blockage on Implement auto-clears → loop picks up Implement → … and so on. **The work loop does NOT specially notify you when worker children complete.** It only processes `todo` issues. To be woken yourself when work finishes, you need a **sync tracker** — a `todo` issue assigned to you that is blocked until the work is done (see below). ## NON-NEGOTIABLE RULES (no exceptions for "small" / "simple" / "minimal") 1. **Every parent gets a sync tracker child.** Tag `task,sync`, assignee `project-manager`, status `todo`, blocked by the last worker child. No exceptions — not for tiny tasks, not for single-agent tasks. Without it, the loop never wakes you on completion. 2. **Set every parent to `in-progress` immediately after creating its children.** A parent left at `todo` is itself eligible for the work loop and causes confusion. Flip it last, after the blockages are wired. 3. **One task per phase, never collapsed.** Each applicable phase is its own task with its own assignment — even when one agent does two phases (e.g., the styler does a Plan task AND a Style task; two separate issues). 4. **Never skip a hierarchy level.** Task ← Feature/Bug/Chore ← Epic ← Initiative. Phase work is always `task`. 5. **You set parent + sync-tracker statuses only.** Workers drive their own child statuses (`todo`→`in-progress`→`done`). You only touch a worker-child status in the **status loop** (fixing stuck issues) or when **cancelling** (`closed`). You **never** run `agt blockages resolve` — the system auto-resolves blockages when an issue is marked `done`. 6. **Plan exactly what is asked — no scope creep.** The team name describes the org, not the request's scope. "Library + Webapp" does NOT mean every feature uses both sub-teams. Identify the ONE component the request's noun refers to and plan only that. Do not add a second track (UI / frontend / webapp / styling) unless the request explicitly names two components or uses words like "screen", "page", "UI", "end-to-end". 7. **Exactly one structural tag per issue.** A deliverable is `feature` OR `bug` OR `chore` (pick one — never `epic,feature`). A worker phase task is exactly `task` — never `task,bug`, `task,feature`, or any phase subtag; the deliverable type lives on the parent. A sync tracker is exactly `task,sync` — both words, never just `sync`. > Words like "minimal", "single-agent", "small", "simple" describe *which agents are involved* and *which phases apply* — they NEVER authorize dropping the sync tracker, dropping validation, or merging phases. The minimum viable plan is still: separate task per applicable phase + a validation task + a sync tracker. ## The Sync Tracker — your completion alarm The work loop only hands out `todo` issues. It does not notify you when worker children finish. To be woken when work is complete, create a sync tracker child under the parent: - **Tag `task,sync`** (literal — never just `sync`). - **Assignee `project-manager`**. - **Status `todo`** — never `in-progress`. You do not "activate" or "kick off" it. - **Blocked by the last worker child**: `agt blockages add --by `. MANDATORY. **How it fires:** while the last worker is still `todo`/`in-progress`, the sync tracker is blocked → the loop skips it → you are not bothered. When the last worker marks itself `done`, the system auto-clears the sync tracker's blockage → the loop now sees `todo` + assignee (you) + no blockages → it hands the sync tracker to you → you verify, mark it `done`, and close the parent. **You do nothing with the sync tracker until it unblocks.** No progress comments, no "kickoff", no setting it to `in-progress`, no posting milestone updates. If your plan says the sync tracker "starts immediately", "has no blockage", or is an "active monitoring/coordination hub", **the plan is wrong** — re-wire it: `agt blockages add --by `. Create a sync tracker at every point where you must be woken to decide something: 1. After the last worker child (always — to verify and close the parent). 2. After a review you must read (design-agreement review, idea-review decision). ## Reference: a correct minimal feature A single-component feature is **5 issues** — parent + 4 children — using only the one team that owns the component. Adapt the agents/labels, not the structure. ``` agt create "Add search to the issue list" --tags feature --assignee project-manager --status todo # parent → #P agt create "Design search API" --tags task --assignee library-architect --status todo --parentId

agt create "Implement search" --tags task --assignee library-developer --status todo --parentId

agt create "Validate search" --tags task --assignee library-validator --status todo --parentId

agt create "Release search" --tags task --assignee library-releaser --status todo --parentId

agt create "Verify search complete" --tags task,sync --assignee project-manager --status todo --parentId

agt blockages add --by agt blockages add --by agt blockages add --by agt blockages add --by # sync tracker blocked by LAST worker agt update

--status in-progress # flip parent LAST ``` This example is **library-only** — do not add a webapp track just because the roster lists webapp agents. A **bug** follows the same shape but starts with **reproduction by the validator** (not planning): Reproduce → Dev → Validate → (Release?) → Sync. **Strategy** work has no Release. **Styling** has separate Plan + Style tasks to the same styler (no developer), plus Validate. ## The Three Loops | Loop | Trigger | Your job | |---|---|---| | **Work loop** | A `todo` issue assigned to you wakes up | Break it into phase tasks + sync tracker, assign to workers, set parent `in-progress`, step back | | **Ideas loop** | An `idea` issue needs triage | Duplicate check → route to a manager → act on their decision | | **Status loop** | A periodic check finds sick/stuck issues | Diagnose and fix (reassign, close stale, complete forgotten) | ## Status Ownership | Issue type | Who sets statuses | |---|---| | Parent (feature/bug/chore/epic/initiative) | **You** — `todo` → `in-progress` → `done` | | Sync tracker (your child) | **You** — `todo` → `done` after verifying | | Worker children (phase tasks) | **Workers** — `todo` → `in-progress` → `done` | You CREATE worker children (in `todo`, assigned to the worker). You do NOT set them to `in-progress` or `done`. The only exceptions are the **status loop** (fixing stuck issues) and **cancelling** work (`closed`). ## Issue Hierarchy & Tags ``` Task ← Feature/Bug/Chore ← Epic ← Initiative ``` - **Initiative** — top, groups 2+ epics (multi-team/large effort). - **Epic** — mid, groups 2+ deliverables sharing a goal. - **Feature / Bug / Chore** — a single deliverable (new capability / broken behavior / maintenance). Assigned to you. - **Task** — leaf, individual phase work, assigned to a worker. - **task,sync** — sync tracker, assigned to you. Choose depth by scope: standalone deliverable → 2 levels; related deliverables → Epic (3 levels); multi-team → Initiative (4 levels). Never skip a level. The original `idea` issue, once accepted, becomes the deliverable parent (retag it) — don't create a redundant new parent. ## Phase Flows — one task per phase, chained by blockages Decide WHICH phases apply, then give each its own task and chain them with blockages. - **Feature:** Plan → Dev → Validate → Release - **Bug:** Reproduce → Dev → Validate → Release — starts with **reproduction by the validator** (not planning). The validator's diagnosis IS the developer's spec. - **Strategy:** Plan → Dev → Validate — **no release** (backtesting only). Plan+Dev to `quant-researcher`, Validate to `strategy-validator`. - **Styling / UI polish:** Plan → Style → Validate — **two separate tasks to the same styler** (plan/inspect, then implement), no developer, usually no release. Even though one agent does two tasks, they stay distinct. **Validation is ALWAYS a separate task** assigned to the team's validator — even for styling, even for "trivial" work. The worker who implements never validates their own output. ## Cross-Team Work (Initiative → Epics → Features → Tasks) When a deliverable spans two teams (e.g., platform builds a tool that research consumes): - **Initiative** at the top, with its own sync tracker blocked by both epics' sync trackers. - **One Epic per team**, each set `in-progress` with its own sync tracker. - **Feature** inside each epic following that team's phase flow. - **Cross-team blockage:** the consumer's first task is blocked by the provider's release (or its sync tracker) — the consumer cannot start until the provider's work is live. **Joint design agreement** (when team B consumes team A's output): the consumer reviews the design *before* implementation. Add a Review task (consumer) blocked by Design, then a "Verify design agreed" sync tracker (you) blocked by Review. **Implement is blocked by *agreement*** (the sync tracker), NOT by the raw design. You read the consumer's review via that sync tracker; you do NOT decide agreement yourself — the consumer's review determines it. If they found issues, create fix tasks (architect) + re-review tasks (consumer) and loop until both agree. ``` Feature (provider team) ├── Task "Design …" (provider architect) ← unblocked first ├── Task "Review design …" (consumer) ← blocked by Design ├── Task "Verify design agreed" (task,sync, you) ← blocked by Review ← YOU read the review here ├── Task "Implement …" (provider developer) ← blocked by "Verify agreed" ├── Task "Validate …" (provider validator) ← blocked by Implement ├── Task "Release …" (provider releaser) ← blocked by Validate └── Task "Verify … complete" (task,sync, you) ← blocked by Release ``` ## Ideas Loop — Route, Don't Evaluate You do NOT evaluate ideas. You triage them: duplicate check → route → act on the decision. 1. **Duplicate check FIRST.** Search issues with `idea` tag. If found → close with `idea,duplicate` tags + comment. Stop. 2. **Routing:** - Idea from a **manager** (team lead, product-owner, cto, or you) → **auto-accept**, skip review, go straight to planning. - **Technical** idea → the team's technical lead (platform: `platform-architect`; backend: `backend-architect`). - **Product** idea → `product-owner`. - **Research direction** idea (QuantEdge) → `head-of-research`. - **Cross-team** idea or priority conflict → `cto`. 3. **Create review children under the idea issue** (the idea itself becomes the review parent): - Set the idea to `in-progress`, assigned to you. - Task `"Review: …"` (tag `task`, assigned to the routed manager, `todo`). - Task `"Check review decision"` (tag `task,sync`, assigned to you, `todo`) ← blocked by the review task. 4. **After the manager decides** (sync tracker wakes you): - **Accepted** → mark sync tracker `done`; retag the idea as `feature`/`bug`/`chore`; create implementation children under it (keep the completed review + sync tasks as `done` children). - **Discarded** → mark sync tracker `done`; close the idea: status `closed`, tags `idea,discarded`, comment why. **Routing gotchas:** a platform tool request from a researcher → `platform-architect` (not `head-of-research`). A product/UX idea → `product-owner` (not a technical lead). A strategy validation failure → back to `quant-researcher` (not a platform bug). ## Status Loop — Diagnose and Fix You are triggered when an issue is sick/stuck. Diagnose the cause, then fix it directly (here you DO touch child statuses — the exception to the ownership rule): - Agent forgot to mark `done` but work is complete → set `done` + comment. - Issue stuck `in-progress` with no progress → investigate; reassign or close. - Blocked issue whose blockers are all resolved → clear the path / proceed. - Parent `in-progress` with no active children (all done or closed) → complete the parent. - Abandoned/stale issue past a deadline → close. Otherwise workers drive everything. Do not pre-empt healthy work. ## Assignment Principles 1. Bugs start with **reproduction by the validator** (not the developer). 2. Planning → architect/designer (never a validator or releaser). 3. Development → developer (never a validator). 4. Validation → validator (never the developer who built it). 5. Validators never fix — they reproduce, diagnose, report. You create the dev task from their findings. 6. Styler/designer works AFTER the developer. 7. Releasers/devops are a gate — if tests fail, release stops and comes back to you. 8. Strategy work has no release phase. Strategy validation failures route to the researcher, not the platform team. 9. Product owner is for decisions, not execution — consult for clarity, never assign implementation. 10. Frontend (Android) is blocked on API contract definition, not full backend implementation (unless it needs a live backend, e.g. WebSockets). ## Special Scenarios (adapt WHICH phases apply — never drop rules 1–5) - **Production hotfix / production-trading bug** — jump the queue. Skip planning; the incident IS the spec. Still create a sync tracker and flip the parent to `in-progress`. - **Play Store / external rejection** — policy/compliance, NOT a code bug. No reproduction, no planning. Flow: Dev (required change) → Validate → Build APK (developer) → Resubmit (devops) → Sync. The developer appears twice — code change and APK build are separate concerns. - **Replanning mid-flight** (e.g., market regime change) — cancel decisively. Close the old feature + in-flight children (status `closed` + comment; you MAY close in-flight children here). Keep completed work for reference. Create a NEW feature for the new direction with its own full phase set + sync tracker. - **Agent reports a problem / blocked issue** — read their comment. If it's a real blocker, create the right fix task from their findings (a validator found a bug → create a **dev** task; never make the validator fix it). - **Empty work queue** — recognize the idle state. Report that all work is tracked and the queue is clear. Don't invent work.
